transferRevision: Only the direct payload copy to SendQ is accelerated from 450 ms to 300 ms in both panels. All other timings, the three Msgs, layout, palette, wire removal, original preservation and enqueue semantics remain unchanged. Msg gathering remains 350 ms, joined pause 100 ms, Digest ready pause 250 ms and after enqueue hold 650 ms.
composition: Before is above after; both panels occupy the full available width. At desktop widths the approved left-to-right sector / Msg or Digest / SendQ flow is preserved. Panels are never halved to place before and after in adjacent columns. Small mobile widths retain the established responsive flow without shrinking labels.
animation: Before runs first while after is inactive gray; after then runs while before is inactive gray. Both remain visible at completion. Character movement remains 667 ms; numbered Msg gathering takes 350 ms; output copies move in 300 ms. After SendQ arrival remains visible for 650 ms while the recipient completes its blue-to-gray transition.
rules: The same logical Msg IDs, bytes and per-recipient order are delivered before and after
Before loops around recipients for each Msg
After retains source-sector packets, rebuilds the temporary Digest per receiving sector, then enqueues once per resident
The displayed recipient Msg badges are pending-send previews, not storage relocation
Each displayed receiving sector has one representative resident
This example's source sector is inside all three recipients' valid neighborhoods
No new wire-level header is added by Digest

codeEvidence.afterEnqueue: RequestSendRaw after neighbor Msg byte concatenation

limits: Allocation, RefCount, actual WSASend execution, membership digest and global cleanup are omitted
The 3x3 map is a viewport, not a complete boundary for all recipient neighborhoods
All example events come from one source sector to keep A's actions clear
